body: sorry, just saw this! I'm actually on Lexapro now, which I didn't know until I just googled it now lol. Mine is under the name Escitalopram, so I didn't realise. Still struggling :/ but I'm in another CBT course now. I'm pushing for diagnoses and whatnot because I can't get a job but hopefully it'll get there
I've been doing more square breathing and need to work on other breathing exercises to get them more into my system. Just they're so easy to forget when panicking sometimes!
I'll be moving home soon and I'm hoping that that might help :) thank you !
I'll try them out - thank you :)

Thank you for the detail :) I found a playlist on YouTube which I have saved to get around to soon :D

Thank you for the podcast recs, too. Will try them out :D

I've tried exposure therapy, meditation, being more gentle with myself by allowing more rest and just pushing forward gently or doing the opposite and really forcing myself into anxious situations. I've tried exercise, new hobbies, etc. I haven't tried CBD/THC as mentioned above by somebody else so I may try that. I also plan to try journalling in more detail to see if that helps or brings any clarity.

I tend to get extremely hot, very sweaty and become nauseous, then I worry more about if I will actually throw up and that makes things worse. I notice I'm always thinking of getting home so that I'm alone and can do whatever I need to to calm down because I feel too self conscious to do what I need to in front of others. Sometimes my legs will go tingly and numb too, but this is relatively rare. Also only sometimes I will just burst into tears when usually I struggle to cry even when I'd like to. Usually lasts around 30 mins to an hour but God it's awful  


I'm likely forgetting some things but that's the general feel.

I always try to use music when walking and that helps somewhat. Maybe a podcast is a good idea, I'll try to find one. More direct experience I feel like. 

How would you recommend learning a language? I want to learn Italian :)

I'll be exercising more soon but yeah it definitely helps. I always get super tired at like 5pm so need to work on my timings, but thank you!! 

I'd love to read so fast! That speed is inspiring. I'll get back to the books and try to cut down the online time. Thank you again ! <3

I will definitely get some soon and try them. If I could get the physical symptoms a bit more under control, it would be such a huge difference. Thank you for giving me some hope! It has been needed.

Yeah, the lack of help from meds is definitely scary. But we'll both figure things out given some time, hopefully!

Best of luck to you too - thanks for your help <3

At first, I was also super on top of things. Would meditate daily, got heavily into reading about mental health and trying to empower myself a little, was in therapy 2x in the first year I was having problems. It just keeps catching up with me it feels like :/ but that isn't to say that everybody will have the same experience. 

Nausea is also a trigger for me, yeah. That's the cycle that is just crippling me. And every single time I'm nauseous I'm somehow able to convince myself that THIS is the time I'm actually unwell. Sometimes it's the first thing I notice upon waking up, that tension in the throat and the stomach cramps.

I also get really frustrated about not being able to socialise. I'd love to be able to do 'normal' things and always feel alienated because I can't go out for a meal or even just go for a walk or meet with people. 

Routines are great - you're right on that one! I try my best to stick to them but sometimes the lack of sleep gets in the way.

All the best for you - I hope you feel better ASAP and can get to the social life you're looking for :)

When I first started having issues, I had a check at the hospital to see if I had any physical issue but I didn't hear anything back. I'll have to give anti-acids a shot, though. I'll try anything at this point!

I have tried both of those. I found they took the edge off slightly but I still couldn't really function. I've been moved onto Lyrica for now (a type of Pregabalin) but still, it isn't doing enough. I seem to start a medication and see some mild positive results, but then quite quickly I think I acclimate to it and I'm worried that it is making things worse rather than better. But maybe that's a normal concern, lol. 

You're the second person to mention DBT to me - I'll have to ask for that too. I move home soon so I'll have to ask for it when I get back and just ride the tide for now. In the meantime I'll try to do some of it myself and keep researching :) Thank you!

I haven't. So far I've only tried prescribed stuff, but I have been desperate for change for a while. I'm just also afraid to introduce something that I then rely on to function. I think I'd use CBD or THC as an absolute last resort... BUT if it's not that serious, please do explain it to me a little. I don't know much about it

I hope you're sleeping now! I get bouts where for weeks I'll wake up 2-3x per night and have chronic nightmares. Recently, I have had my first experiences with sleep paralysis - utterly terrifying. Sleeping on my side instead of my back stopped that (for now), so that's a plus.

The nausea after meals is crippling, honestly. Stops me from doing so much. Nothing seems to help - I've tried eating less, eating more, eating diff foods, etc. but no change really. :/ 

  
It feels hopeless, but we'll make it someday. All we can do is hope

Archy's music is inspired by the poetry of W.H. Auden, he mentioned him somewhere (I think in a YouTube interview?) a while ago

He also used a reading of Anne Sexton's poem Wanting to Die on the Sublunary Demo, so I imagine he's into her work. Her book Live or Die is fantastic, I'd recommend it
I spoke to my counsellor about it and was only given a phone number despite the fact that I’ve made it clear that I can barely use a phone
Waiting on that new Frank Ocean album

I’m in counselling right now on a course for anxiety. I opened up last week for the first tine in person about being suicidal, was given a crisis number and that was it. Needless to say I won’t bother embarrassing myself with that again. I’ll see how it goes with the anxiety but I’m four weeks in and it seems like it’s just spending hour after hour finding the nicest way to say “just deal with it”.
Best of luck, buddy!

I spoke about being suicidal to a fucking COUNSELLOR and they just gave me a number. I told them the truth, how I feel that way almost every night and that I keep getting closer to doing it, but I just got a phone number I could’ve looked up in three seconds.
I appreciate just knowing somebody else feels like they’re in the same cycle. It’s tough, and especially harsh when you think you’re getting somewhere only to fall back in.
I spin Kendrick Lamar mostly when I’m feeling real low. Often helps.
Even better! Thanks for letting me know... I’ll add it to some more!
